title: Mahalabia Milk Pudding with Pistachios
summary: A smooth, delicately scented milk pudding set in moulds, turned out and topped with chopped pistachios.
equipment: 6 x 150 ml moulds or cups, rinsed with cold water

ingredients.note: crush with a pinch of the sugar

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: warm two-thirds of the milk with the sugar and mastic over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.

steps.title: Slurry
steps.text: whisk the cornflour into the remaining cold milk until no lumps remain. Cold milk stops the cornflour forming lumps.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: pour the slurry slowly into the pan, stirring constantly with the spoon and scraping the base, and cook 6-8 min until it boils and turns thick and glossy. The cornflour needs to boil to thicken fully.

steps.title: Mould
steps.text: pour at once into the wet moulds, cool 1 h, then cover and chill at least 3 h until firm. Wet moulds help the pudding slip out.

steps.title: Turn out
steps.text: loosen the edges with a knife, invert onto plates and top with a mound of chopped pistachios.

tips: A common mistake is stopping before it boils; the pudding will not set firmly enough to turn out.
Mastic gives a gentle pine flavour; leave it out if you cannot find it.
For a softer pudding, set it in glasses and do not turn it out.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Cover and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days. Add the pistachios just before serving.
